title: The proper Hilbert presheaf is the Quot presheaf of the structure sheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:A\to B$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Assume that $a$ is of finite presentation. Use the space morphism properties, module conventions and Quot presheaf of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. For a scheme $T\to B$, let $\mathcal H_{A/B}(T)$ be the set of closed subspaces $i:D\hookrightarrow A_T$ with $D\to T$ proper, flat and of finite presentation, identified up to isomorphism of closed immersions over $A_T$; transitions are inverse images of closed subspaces. The assignment $[i:D\hookrightarrow A_T]\mapsto[\mathcal O_{A_T}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_D]$ is a bijection $\mathcal H_{A/B}(T)\simeq\operatorname{Quot}_{\mathcal O_A/A/B}(T)$. Its inverse takes a quotient to the closed subspace cut out by its kernel ideal. These bijections commute with every scheme base change $T\prime\to T$ over $B$, including non-flat base changes, and hence form a natural isomorphism of presheaves over $B$.

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T\to B$ and write $X=A_T$. By arbitrary base-change stability, $X\to T$ is of finite presentation. For a Hilbert object $i:D\hookrightarrow X$, both $D\to T$ and $X\to T$ are locally of finite presentation, hence the latter is locally of finite type. Relative finite-presentation permanence therefore makes $i$ locally of finite presentation. Apply the closed-structure criterion: $i$ is of finite presentation and $i_*\mathcal O_D$ is a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module.

The closed-pushforward theorem makes $q_i:\mathcal O_X\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_D$ surjective with quasi-coherent target. The relative-flatness lemma makes its target flat over $T$ because $D\to T$ is flat. Its proper carrier is $D$ itself, with the finite type module $\mathcal O_D$, generated locally by $1$. Thus all the target conditions in the Quot definition hold. An isomorphism of closed immersions induces an isomorphism of these quotient modules intertwining $q_i$, so this construction is defined on the specified isomorphism classes.

Conversely take a Quot object $q:\mathcal O_X\twoheadrightarrow Q$. Its kernel $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent by closure of quasi-coherent modules under kernels. It is an ideal: $q(ab)=a q(b)=0$ whenever $q(b)=0$. The ideal correspondence constructs a unique closed subspace $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ with ideal $\mathcal I$. The surjection identifies $Q$ with $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I\simeq i_*\mathcal O_D$ compatibly with $q$. The module $Q$ is of finite presentation, so the closed-structure criterion makes $i$ of finite presentation; composition with $X\to T$ makes $D\to T$ of finite presentation.

The relative-flatness lemma applied to $Q\simeq i_*\mathcal O_D$ gives flatness of $D\to T$. Since $X\to T$ is of finite presentation, it is locally of finite type, as required for the proper-carrier lemma. The Quot condition gives a proper closed carrier for $Q$; that lemma identifies its scheme-theoretic support with $D$ and makes $D\to T$ proper. This proves that the inverse construction lands in the Hilbert set without any Noetherian hypothesis.

An isomorphism of quotients intertwining their maps from $\mathcal O_X$ gives equal kernels, hence equal closed-subspace classes by the ideal correspondence. Starting with $i$ returns its kernel ideal and then its original closed-subspace class. Starting with $q$ returns $\mathcal O_X\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_X/\ker q$, which is isomorphic to $q$ by the induced quotient isomorphism. Thus the two maps on isomorphism classes are mutually inverse.

Let $T\prime\to T$ be any scheme morphism over $B$ and $p:X\prime=A_{T\prime}\to X$. The ideal correspondence supplies $p^*(i_*\mathcal O_D)\simeq i\prime_*\mathcal O_{D\prime}$, preserving the quotient map, where $D\prime=D\times_TT\prime$. Hence the forward assignment commutes with the transition maps. Both transitions are defined: flatness, properness and finite presentation of $D\to T$ persist by arbitrary base change, and the Quot transitions are those in its definition. No exactness on the left of a pulled-back ideal sequence is asserted: the new ideal is the image of $p^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{X\prime}$. Since the forward maps are bijective, their inverse maps also commute with transitions (apply the bijective forward map on $T\prime$ to both sides). Thus the bijections give the claimed natural isomorphism, including non-flat base change.

lean.statement: theorem properHilbert_is_quot (a : A ⟶ B) (ha : ProperQuotFinitePresentation a) : ∃ unitIso : ∀ T : ProperQuotTest B, (moduleTensorPullback (properQuotFst a T)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit A.structureSheaf) ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (properQuotFibre a T).structureSheaf, (∀ T : ProperQuotTest B, (unitIso T).hom = ((moduleTensorAdjunction (properQuotFst a T)).homEquiv _ _).symm (moduleStructureMap (properQuotFst a T))) ∧ ∃ e : properHilbertFunctor a ≅ properQuotFunctor a ha (hilbertStructureModule A), (∀ (T : ProperQuotTest B) (C : ProperHilbertFamily a T), ∃ q : ProperQuotient a (SheafOfModules.unit A.structureSheaf) T, e.hom.app (op T) C = Quot.mk _ q ∧ ∃ θ : q.target ≅ (moduleDirectImage C.val.val.arrow).obj (SheafOfModules.unit (C.val.val : AlgebraicSpace S).structureSheaf), q.quotient ≫ θ.hom = (unitIso T).hom ≫ moduleStructureMap C.val.val.arrow) ∧ (∀ (T : ProperQuotTest B) (q : ProperQuotient a (SheafOfModules.unit A.structureSheaf) T), kernelSubobject ((unitIso T).inv ≫ q.quotient) = kernelSubobject (moduleStructureMap (e.inv.app (op T) (Quot.mk _ q)).val.val.arrow))
